question: In a patient with proptosis and an orbital mass, signs that favour malignancy over a benign lesion include rapid onset (weeks), irregular poorly-defined margins on imaging, pain, and bony erosion on CT.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The malignant orbital tumour red flag triad is: rapid onset + pain + bony destruction on CT. Benign lesions (cavernous haemangioma, dermoid cyst, lacrimal gland pleomorphic adenoma) typically show smooth, well-defined margins, remodel (not erode) bone, and produce slowly progressive painless proptosis. Irregular margins + bone erosion = malignancy until proven otherwise.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Red flags for malignant orbital tumour: (1) rapid onset proptosis (weeks, not months/years); (2) pain — benign lesions like cavernous haemangioma are typically painless; (3) irregular, poorly-defined or infiltrative margins on CT/MRI; (4) bony erosion or destruction (malignancy invades bone; most benign lesions displace or remodel but do not destroy it); (5) associated lymphadenopathy or systemic symptoms. These features mandate urgent referral for CT-guided biopsy and oncological review.
